title: Victor Lagno arXiv paper backs Pais room-temperature superconductor
summary: Salvatore Pais tells of Victor Lagno arXiv paper backs Pais room-temperature superconductor, about unspecified at Russian Academy of Sciences, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: he showed that my room temperature superc conductor from a mechanism point of view could work and yet the the patent examiner just refused to grant the patent.

plain: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for unusual patents, tells Jesse Michels's podcast that he applied to patent a superconductor that works at room temperature, meaning a material that carries electricity with no loss without being chilled. Pais says a scientist named Victor Lagno, of the Russian Academy of Sciences, posted a paper on arXiv, a public site for science papers, showing his idea could work in principle. Even so, Pais says, the patent examiner refused to grant the patent.
